objects.alt: An empty station platform at night: iron columns, a clock at 11:59, a sign saying 13, a bench with a jack-o'-lantern, a gas lamp

objects.text: Platform 13
Halloween. You missed the last bus home. The station clock says 11:59, and far down the line, a light is coming.

objects.alt: The station clock, one minute to midnight

objects.text: The timetable

LAST BUS ........ 11:45
LAST TRAIN ...... none

Underneath, someone has written in silver ink that seems to move:

MIDNIGHT TRAIN .. 12:00
ALL STOPS. NO RETURNS.

objects.alt: A black steam train with lit windows stands at the platform; pale passengers look out; one door is open
Steam rises from the chimney (animated)

objects.text: The Midnight Train
At the last stroke of twelve a black train rolls in without a sound. One door slides open. Warm light spills out.

objects.alt: Inside a carriage: red velvet seats down both sides, brass lamps, night outside, pale passengers in the seats

objects.text: Carriage One
Velvet seats, brass lamps, and passengers who are not quite there. Nobody looks up. The train begins to move.
» Look out of the window

objects.alt: A carriage window framed in wood and red velvet curtains
Hills, a village and telegraph poles slide past under the moon (animated)

objects.text: The Window
Your town slides past, then fields, then hills you have never seen. The train makes no sound at all. You feel sleepy.

objects.alt: The front of the carriage: wood panels, a route map, and the door to the engine with a round window full of firelight
The conductor: a tall pale ghost in a navy coat and a silver-banded cap

objects.text: The Conductor
A tall man in a silver-banded cap blocks the door to the engine. His face is the colour of moonlight. “Tickets, please.”
You have no ticket. He frowns.
He gave you a little lantern.

objects.alt: Mortimer the conductor

objects.text: Mortimer

“I have run this line every Halloween for a hundred years. My passengers all lost their way home, long ago.

Find a ticket before the last stop, or you will ride with us forever. Here. It is dark in the luggage van.”

objects.alt: A dining car: a table with white linen, a red lamp, tea for two, and a wide window onto the night
Mrs. Pell, an old lady ghost in a knitted shawl, squinting
Mrs. Pell's old ticket, lying on the tablecloth

objects.text: The Dining Car
An old lady in a knitted shawl squints at a menu held upside down. “I can't read a thing,” she sighs.
She needs her spectacles.
She gives you her old ticket!

objects.alt: Mrs. Pell with her knitting

objects.text: Mrs. Pell

“I bought this ticket in 1952 to visit my sister. I fell asleep and woke up on the wrong train.

It is no use to me now. Find my spectacles and it's yours, dear. I think the little boy was playing with them.”

objects.alt: A sleeper compartment: two bunks with quilts, a ladder, a round window with the moon, a little night light
Pip, a ghost boy in a nightshirt, holding a pair of spectacles

objects.text: The Sleeper Car
A boy in a nightshirt sits on the bottom bunk, wide awake. Something round and glassy glints in his hands.
He won't swap without his music box.
He swaps it for the spectacles!

objects.alt: Pip, holding the spectacles

objects.text: Pip

“I can't sleep without my music box. It plays the song my mum used to hum.

I left it in the luggage van, but it's dark in there, and Biscuit growls at the dark.”

objects.alt: A dark luggage van: a steamer trunk, a suitcase, a hatbox, a crate marked FRAGILE, an empty birdcage, moonlight through the door
Biscuit, a ghost dog with one floppy ear, peeking out from behind the crate
A small wooden music box on the trunk

objects.text: The Luggage Van
Trunks and cages rattle in the dark. Two pale eyes shine from behind a crate. Something growls, softly.
Too dark. The growling gets louder.
Biscuit wags. A music box!
» Pat the dog

objects.alt: Biscuit, wagging

objects.text: Biscuit

A ghost dog with one floppy ear and a brass tag that says BISCUIT.

He was the guard's dog, long ago, and he still guards everybody's luggage. He sniffs your hand, decides you are all right, and rolls over.

objects.alt: The ticket, punched HOME

objects.text: Punched!

Mortimer turns the old ticket over in his long fingers, and smiles for the first time.

Click. HOME.

“Next stop, your street. Go and say goodbye to your friends.”

objects.alt: The train crosses a tall stone viaduct in front of a huge moon, every window lit, small figures waving

objects.text: The High Bridge
The train swings out over the high bridge. Mrs. Pell, Pip and Biscuit crowd the windows to wave goodbye.

objects.alt: Your street at dawn; the train climbs into the sky trailing gold steam above the rooftops

objects.text: Home
At dawn the train sets you down at your own front door, then climbs into the sky. In your pocket: a ticket punched HOME. The end.

objects.alt: A pale station made of fog with a sign reading LAST STOP and grey figures waiting

objects.text: The Last Stop
You wake at a station made of fog. Mortimer tips his cap. “No ticket? Then welcome aboard, forever.” The end.
